- middleware/set_headers.go:19-22 — snapshot: `cfg` is a new `http.Header`; each key is canonicalized with `http.CanonicalHeaderKey` (same semantics as `textproto.CanonicalMIMEHeaderKey`, which `Header.Set` uses) and each value slice is deep-copied via `append([]string(nil), values...)`.

- middleware/content_type.go:9-11 — `SetHeader` returns `SetHeaders(http.Header{key: []string{value}})`, delegating replacement/canonicalization; `AllowContentType` unchanged and still uses both imports.

what: `middleware.SetHeaders(headers http.Header) func(http.Handler) http.Handler` implemented in a new file with factory-time snapshot (map and value slices), canonicalized names, per-request replacement of configured headers, preservation of unlisted headers, and per-request fresh value slices. `middleware.SetHeader` now delegates to `SetHeaders`. New test file covers the required behaviors.

paths:
- middleware/set_headers.go (new)
- middleware/content_type.go (SetHeader refactored)
- middleware/set_headers_test.go (new)

facts:
- middleware/set_headers.go:12-17 — `len(headers) == 0` path returns `func(next){ return next }`, a true no-op for nil and empty input.
- middleware/set_headers.go:19-22 — snapshot: `cfg` is a new `http.Header`; each key is canonicalized with `http.CanonicalHeaderKey` (same semantics as `textproto.CanonicalMIMEHeaderKey`, which `Header.Set` uses) and each value slice is deep-copied via `append([]string(nil), values...)`.
- middleware/set_headers.go:24-31 — per request: `h := w.Header()`, then `h[name] = append([]string(nil), values...)` for each configured name, replacing that name's existing values while leaving unlisted headers untouched, then `next.ServeHTTP`.
- middleware/content_type.go:9-11 — `SetHeader` returns `SetHeaders(http.Header{key: []string{value}})`, delegating replacement/canonicalization; `AllowContentType` unchanged and still uses both imports.
- middleware/set_headers_test.go:10-33 — nil/empty identity check via `reflect.ValueOf(...).Pointer()` (valid because the no-op path returns `next` itself, not a wrapper).
- middleware/set_headers_test.go:35-77 — snapshot and replacement: mutating the caller's map/slice after factory creation does not leak; pre-existing matching key is replaced, non-matching pre-existing and downstream-set headers survive.
- middleware/set_headers_test.go:79-105 — per-request fresh slices: tampering with the first response's `X-Multi` slice doesn't affect the second request.
- middleware/set_headers_test.go:107-120 — `SetHeader` delegation replaces an existing value.
- get_diagnostics clean on middleware/set_headers.go, middleware/content_type.go, middleware/set_headers_test.go.

reasoning: The implementation matches the design: a single `cfg` built and copied at factory time, then only per-request value copies are written into the response header map. Direct map assignment (`h[name] = ...`) gives exact replacement semantics and preserves unlisted keys. Delegating `SetHeader` keeps the single-key path on the same code path, at the cost of a minor empty-key behavior change noted below.

test_plan:
- `go test ./middleware/...` — all existing plus the four new tests pass; diagnostics clean.
- Case empty/nil input: `SetHeaders(nil)(next) == next` and `SetHeaders(http.Header{})(next) == next`.
- Case snapshot: mutate the source `http.Header` and one of its slices after `SetHeaders(source)`; response still contains the original keys/values, not the mutations.
- Case replacement/preservation: pre-set a configured header and an unrelated header; after serving, configured header holds all supplied values and the unrelated header is unchanged.
- Case per-request copy: mutate the response's header value slice inside/after the first request; a second request still gets the original values.
- Case delegation: `SetHeader("X-Test","new")` over an existing `X-Test: old`.

verdict: approve

leftover: `middleware/set_headers.go` and `middleware/set_headers_test.go` are untracked in the worktree (visible via git_status, not git_diff). Minor behavior edge: the old `SetHeader` used `w.Header().Set(key, value)`, which in net/http returns early when `key == ""`, so `SetHeader("", v)` was a silent no-op; the delegated version now sets an empty-named header entry. Non-empty-key behavior is equivalent. If strict preservation of the empty-key no-op is required, guard it in `SetHeader`; otherwise low severity, likely out of scope.

reasoning: The implementation matches the design: a single `cfg` built and copied at factory time, then only per-request value copies are written into the response header map. Direct map assignment (`h[name] = ...`) gives exact replacement semantics and preserves unlisted keys. Delegating `SetHeader` keeps the single-key path on the same code path, at the cost of a minor empty-key behavior change noted below.
